gen-dafont-existence-gf-scope-one: Wide, porthole-like counters give Existence an industrial look, with terminals cut well short of each bowl. Scope One, a text serif, spills its open shapes into the space around them, and its stubby ascenders keep the lines tucked and sturdy beneath.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-slabo-13px: Existence is built from parts of matching mass, its lowercase counters round and wide like glass portholes. Slabo 13px, a classic serif, has tall a, e and s forms with generous openings, so extended reading feels bookish and dignified.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum leads with a high, squared-off x-height and a c as open as a bent paperclip. Its text serif dignity gives Existence, with crossbars as fat as its stems, a sturdy industrial partner.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-asap: Franchise packs tall small letters shoulder to shoulder, every stroke one unbroken line weight from terminal to junction. Asap, a sans with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, sits well at modest sizes beneath it.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-epilogue: Franchise stands strong and clean, its tall small letters crowded together with the tips of each c pulled well apart. Epilogue's curvy, wire-thin sans-serif forms loosen things up.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-public-sans: Strong and clean, Franchise crams tall lowercase letters together, and its n arches are as thick as the stems beside them. Public Sans, a sans-serif, brings the hefty, trustworthy lowercase and broad open counters that carry the actual reading.
gen-dafont-franchise-general-sans: Franchise crowds its tall small letters together, with c tips pulled well apart. General Sans, a plain sans with an x-height filling the line, would drown out the heading if the heading were made small.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab, a classic serif, has a visibly gaping c and tall rounded lowercase at any size. Franchise cuts a tighter, stricter figure beside it, its terminals ending at the width they began.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-fauna-one: Literary and dignified, Fauna One keeps a tall middle band with shallow ascenders and descenders. Franchise, bent like wire across each word, gives that classic serif a strong, clean, tightly packed headline to follow.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-glegoo: Refined and editorial, Glegoo, a classic serif, makes big counters in a tall lowercase with wide, unclosed curves. Franchise, with technical-drawing-pen lines and tightly packed letters, does the headline work, and Glegoo handles the reading.
